title: Kotoba audit of the 350 supplied learning and engineering blueprint requirements
sourceScope: The five supplied attachments contain exactly numbered items 1-350. Introductory prose mentions 1,000 instructions, but items 351-1000 were not supplied and are not invented. Original numbered text is retained verbatim.

statusDefinitions.existing: Current source supports the requested behavior within the explicitly stated assessment scope; final execution evidence is reported separately.
statusDefinitions.implemented-local: New local source implements the selected behavior. This label is not a claim of server integration, device-wide support, certification, or completion of the whole blueprint.
statusDefinitions.prepared: A concrete schema, interface, route descriptor, contract, or migration exists, but the live service or database is unconnected.
statusDefinitions.partial: Related behavior exists, but a material part of the literal prescription, coverage, integration, measurement, or validation remains missing.
statusDefinitions.deferred: The requested feature is not implemented. Cited source identifies the closest existing boundary or documented future dependency.
statusDefinitions.intentional-variant: The implemented choice deliberately differs from the literal prescription because of a later instruction, deterministic assessment requirements, local-only scope, accessibility, or stated technical constraints.

scopeDefinitions.existing: Existing local study, interface, assessment, or packaging behavior.
scopeDefinitions.new-local: Selected new local learning, recall, preference, or reward behavior; no external service is implied.
scopeDefinitions.prepared: Concrete preparation for a future backend or hosted integration without connecting it.
scopeDefinitions.server-required: The literal feature requires shared identity, trustworthy transactions, hosting, delivery, analytics, or other unconnected server infrastructure.
scopeDefinitions.asset-or-platform: Completion depends on verified content/assets, expert review, device/platform behavior, or validation not currently available.
scopeDefinitions.mismatch-or-partial: Existing or new behavior intentionally differs from or only partly satisfies the literal prescription.

auditBasis.runtime: The active application is index.html and local classic scripts/styles/assets. The retained React prototype is inactive; runtime use requires no npm install.
auditBasis.selectedScope: Broader local and offline learning features with preparation for a future backend; no actual database connection now.
auditBasis.evidenceConvention: Paths and literal anchors identify source, check suites, assets, references, or contracts. Check references do not assert that a particular suite or device journey was executed by this audit. Source line numbers identify the inspected snapshot; literal anchors are rechecked by check-blueprint.mjs.
auditBasis.newLocalSource: SM2, Learning Lab, optional goals/rewards, speech transcription, comfort preferences, IndexedDB archive, hosted service-worker caching, the shared scheduling service, local data tools, and path review-attention helpers are integrated and verified within the documented local scope. Final execution evidence is recorded separately below; this does not imply that all 350 literal prescriptions are complete.

types.scope: The canonical TypeScript sources and their imported models; the inactive React prototype is excluded.

chrome.scope: Actual packaged controls, relative project subpath, isolated saved state, responsive layout, mouse/touch/keyboard dragging, direct-file use, recall ratings, local cleanup, hosted offline reload of all nine screens, IndexedDB archive and scoped cache opt-out.
chrome.limits: Controlled speech and permission fallbacks do not establish real Japanese voice availability, transcription accuracy, pronunciation scoring, every browser behavior or WCAG certification.

restrictions: 350 provided requirements are audited; the earlier independent 100-item audit remains separate.
Browser speech recognition is editable transcription, not phoneme recognition or pronunciation scoring; an independent microphone waveform does not filter the recognition service.
Browser TTS voice buffers cannot be extracted and cached as generated audio files; available Japanese voices and recognition may depend on the device or network.
No human recording library, verified lexical pitch-accent or radical corpus, hired native-speaker review, or complete textbook chapter/day/point mapping is claimed.
Scheduled reminders with the browser closed, friends, email, leagues, CMS publication, trusted anti-cheat and AI services need unconnected server or platform integrations.
UTC review arithmetic is deterministic, but a local clock is not server authoritative and cannot prevent device time manipulation.
A CEFR crosswalk, universal sub-100ms latency, actual screen-reader conformance, WCAG AAA certification, and legal compliance certification are not established.
No portrait orientation lock is forced; responsive layout and learner accessibility take priority.
Optional hearts never block core learning, and reward participation, reminders, motion and speech remain learner controlled.
Exact requested EF-first SM2 math stays transparent rather than opaque, default pure scheduling has no fuzz, and a 365-day cap is an explicit UI policy.
IP/User-Agent-bound JWTs, guilt-tripping reminders, automatic tree mastery from a brief quiz, and silent conflict overwrites are not introduced.
Original mock results remain raw accuracy, not historical exam papers, official scaled scores, pass predictions or proficiency certification.
A prepared PostgreSQL migration, memory adapter, local/remote port and OpenAPI contract do not imply a deployed server, connected database or production authentication.
The archive is a secondary ordered local snapshot; localStorage remains the canonical save and portable JSON backups remain important.

localPrivacy.browserStatus: passed in the full 62-journey packaged regression and again in the 13-journey final local/offline run
localPrivacy.scope: Aggregate summary export excludes individual answer history and personal text by default. Draft and issue files explicitly contain personal text. Validated subset cleanup leaves canonical assessment, recall and reward records byte-equivalent, bypasses reward reconciliation for this cleanup-only update, rejects stale confirmation, and does not erase downloaded copies. No account, public profile, cloud sync, or legal compliance certification is implied.

pathRecall.browserStatus: passed in the full 62-journey packaged regression and again after the final learner-facing copy update
pathRecall.scope: Gold requires assessed mastery of all linked questions. Review attention starts at 30 elapsed days since successful linked evidence; missing or future dates do not invent a lapse. Review uses existing lesson vocabulary questions, weak evidence first and at most ten distinct words, with the actual count disclosed. Daily nodes contain at most seven words. No reminder clears merely by opening a node or starting practice, and no mastery record is automatically removed.

requirements.userText: Break down all educational material into atomic, discrete skills (e.g., "Present Tense", "Food Vocab").
requirements.assessment: Lessons, grammar points, and small Lab queues use stable discrete content IDs.
requirements.remainingGap: A complete atomic skill taxonomy across the entire bank has not been verified.

requirements.userText: Map these atomic skills to a standardized framework (such as CEFR for languages).
requirements.assessment: The curriculum uses JLPT study levels and verified publisher topic references.
requirements.remainingGap: No validated CEFR crosswalk is provided; JLPT levels are not asserted to be equivalent CEFR levels.

requirements.userText: Introduce a maximum of 3 to 5 new vocabulary words or concepts per lesson to prevent cognitive overload.
requirements.assessment: Learning Lab limits its selected new concepts to 3–5.
requirements.remainingGap: The limit is not enforced across every existing integrated path lesson or library activity.

requirements.userText: Separate the introduction of new vocabulary from the introduction of new complex grammar rules.
requirements.assessment: Lab vocabulary and Culture and usage modes can be chosen separately.
requirements.remainingGap: Integrated path lessons intentionally combine words and grammar; a universal separation is absent.

requirements.userText: Use implicit learning for grammar; show patterns through multiple exercises before explicitly explaining the rule.
requirements.assessment: Examples and exercises accompany explicit grammar attachments and explanations.
requirements.remainingGap: Implicit-before-explicit sequencing is not forced; learners may read a rule immediately.

requirements.userText: Provide short, optional "Guidebooks" or tips for users who prefer reading explicit rules.
requirements.assessment: Grammar detail panels provide explanations, attachments, examples, and reference notes.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Structure lessons so they take no more than 3 to 5 minutes to complete, catering to mobile microlearning.
requirements.assessment: Short Lab lessons offer 3–5 concepts and a stated 3–5 minute target.
requirements.remainingGap: Completion duration depends on the learner and device; a universal five-minute maximum is not measured or enforced.

requirements.userText: Require users to master foundational skills before unlocking advanced tiers.
requirements.assessment: Optional prerequisite guidance identifies earlier skills while advanced study remains accessible.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no compulsory mastery lock; checklist completion is not treated as demonstrated mastery.

requirements.userText: Implement a Spaced Repetition System (SRS) to schedule reviews right before the forgetting curve drops.
requirements.assessment: Explicit 0–5 recall ratings schedule due reviews using deterministic SM2.
requirements.remainingGap: Review timestamps are algorithmic estimates; an individual measured forgetting curve is not available.

requirements.userText: Use an exponential SRS algorithm: if an answer is correct, increase the interval between reviews (e.g., 1 day, 4 days, 10 days, 23 days).
requirements.assessment: The user's later exact EF-first SM2 formula determines increasing successful intervals.
requirements.remainingGap: The illustrative 1/4/10/23 sequence is not hardcoded; successful initial intervals are 1 and 6 days.

requirements.userText: Decrease the SRS interval immediately if the user answers a review question incorrectly.
requirements.assessment: A failed quality 0–2 rating immediately resets repetitions and schedules one day.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Review harder concepts sooner and push back the review dates for concepts the user answers easily.
requirements.assessment: Quality ratings adjust easiness and successive review intervals.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Wait until the very end of a single lesson to present the user with the mistakes they made during that session.
requirements.assessment: Lab lessons collect a final mistake summary; full mocks withhold all feedback until completion.
requirements.remainingGap: Normal practice and Lab checks also show immediate feedback; mistakes are not universally hidden until the end.

requirements.userText: Transition users from passive recognition (multiple choice) to active recall (typing or speaking) as a concept ages.
requirements.assessment: Learners can choose typing, dictation, sentence construction, or revealed flashcard recall.
requirements.remainingGap: No automatic age-based transition from multiple choice to speaking is implemented.

requirements.userText: Use varied exercise formats continuously: sentence translation, fill-in-the-blanks, audio listening, speech pronunciation, and pair-matching.
requirements.assessment: Lab supplies recall, sentence blocks, pair matching, dictation, and optional speech transcription.
requirements.remainingGap: Speech is transcription rather than pronunciation assessment; free sentence translation and conjugation coverage remain limited.

requirements.userText: Integrate text-to-speech AI to dynamically generate audio for all text elements.
requirements.assessment: Listening scripts, dictation, and selected word interactions can use Japanese browser speech.
requirements.remainingGap: Not every text element has audio; browser voices are device dependent rather than a generated neural audio library.

requirements.userText: Ensure audio plays automatically when a new vocabulary word or sentence appears on screen.
requirements.assessment: Automatic word audio is optional and begins after a user interaction.
requirements.remainingGap: Unconditional autoplay is avoided because it can disrupt quiet study and is restricted by browser autoplay policy.

requirements.userText: Provide a "turtle mode" button that plays audio at 50% speed for difficult listening comprehension exercises.
requirements.assessment: Slow study controls halve browser-speech rate or supplied-audio playback rate.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Allow users to completely disable speaking or listening exercises temporarily if they are in a public space.
requirements.assessment: Quiet mode hides audio-dependent Lab activities, disables speech input, and prevents automatic word speech.
requirements.remainingGap: Manual ordinary listening playback is not universally disabled; quiet mode is not a complete all-page exercise gate.

requirements.userText: Design the curriculum progression as a single, linear path to reduce decision fatigue and choice paralysis.
requirements.assessment: Each selected level has an ordered learning path and a resume point.
requirements.remainingGap: Library browsing and level changes remain available; the entire app is not forced into one exclusive path.

requirements.userText: Treat gamification as your core design language, not an overlay; educate *through* games.
requirements.assessment: Friendly cards, a mascot, learning interactions, and optional rewards support the learning flow.
requirements.remainingGap: Whether games form the core pedagogy is a design judgment; optional rewards do not transform every lesson into a game.

requirements.userText: Establish a universal currency, like Experience Points (XP), to reward all in-app actions.
requirements.assessment: Local learning XP rewards supported assessed answers, study, lessons, and due recall.
requirements.remainingGap: Navigation, repeated reveals, and checklist actions intentionally do not earn XP; not all actions are rewarded.

requirements.userText: Award XP immediately upon lesson completion, before the user even closes the summary screen.
requirements.assessment: Reconciliation records eligible lesson or assessed-session rewards immediately on the local update.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Connect all mechanics (streaks, leaderboards, achievements) directly back to the central XP system.
requirements.assessment: Private quests and badges derive from local learning evidence and XP.
requirements.remainingGap: No live leaderboard exists; streak goals can use minutes rather than XP exclusively.

requirements.userText: Utilize the psychological principle of loss aversion by making Streaks a primary retention mechanic.
requirements.assessment: Optional protected streaks encourage a chosen pace without requiring reward participation.
requirements.remainingGap: Loss-aversion pressure is not made the mandatory retention mechanism.

requirements.userText: Display the user's current streak count prominently on the main home screen.
requirements.assessment: The dashboard exposes streak information and optional local motivation progress.
requirements.remainingGap: The optional motivation widget can be hidden; prominence is configurable.

requirements.userText: Reset the streak counter to zero immediately if a user misses their daily goal.
requirements.assessment: The optional local protected streak counts consecutive positive-XP activity days, with freezes for completed missed days.
requirements.remainingGap: It does not reset exclusively according to the selected daily-minute or daily-XP target; freezes can protect a missed day.

requirements.userText: Offer "Streak Freezes" as a structural feature to prevent user churn after a missed day (freezes can extend average 14-day streaks to over 30 days).
requirements.assessment: Earned streak freezes protect completed missed days without inventing learning events.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Allow users to equip a maximum of two streak freezes at a time to maintain a sense of scarcity.
requirements.assessment: The local earned-coin shop limits held freezes to two.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Leverage the psychological weight of losing a streak by allowing users to trade their hard-earned in-app currency for Streak Freezes.
requirements.assessment: Users can buy a freeze with coins earned from learning evidence.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Let users set personalized, achievable daily goals (e.g., 5 to 20 minutes) rather than forcing a universal target that causes consistent failure.
requirements.assessment: Optional goals include adjustable daily study minutes and learning XP.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Calibrate streak maintenance exclusively to the user's personalized daily goal.
requirements.assessment: Adjustable minute and XP goals are displayed separately from the optional protected activity streak.
requirements.remainingGap: Protected streak days currently use positive-XP learning activity, not exclusive satisfaction of the selected goal; the older action streak is also separate.

requirements.userText: Trigger a time-limited XP boost when a user hits a milestone, encouraging immediate re-engagement in that same session.
requirements.assessment: An earned monthly reward or shop purchase supplies an explicitly activated 20-minute XP boost.
requirements.remainingGap: Boosts are not automatically imposed whenever any milestone is reached.

requirements.userText: Implement weekly leaderboards (Leagues) where users compete for XP against 29 other similarly engaged players.
requirements.assessment: Rewards remain private and local; the contract prepares an authenticated future progress boundary.
requirements.remainingGap: No 30-person live weekly league, matchmaking, or server ranking is implemented.

requirements.userText: Create tiered leagues (e.g., Bronze, Silver, Gold, Diamond) with promotion and demotion zones.
requirements.assessment: Bronze, Silver, and Gold are local quest names, not public competitive leagues.
requirements.remainingGap: Live league tiers, promotion, and demotion require an unconnected shared service.

requirements.userText: Reset leaderboards weekly to provide a fresh start and prevent permanent dominance by power users.
requirements.assessment: The future server roadmap distinguishes progress sync from competitive services.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no live leaderboard to reset weekly.

requirements.userText: Award badges and achievements for long-term milestones (e.g., "Learn 1000 words", "365-day streak").
requirements.assessment: Evidence-backed milestone, streak, review, and monthly badges are stored locally.
requirements.remainingGap: The illustrative 1,000-word and 365-day badges are not both supplied. Expanding the word bank alone does not supply those achievement rules.

requirements.userText: Introduce "Friends Quests" that pair users together to complete a shared objective for mutual rewards.
requirements.assessment: Private goals do not simulate another learner or claim shared progress.
requirements.remainingGap: Friend pairing, joint quests, identity, and mutual rewards require shared backend state.

requirements.userText: Hide complex progress metrics behind simple visual indicators like filling rings, crowns, or stars.
requirements.assessment: Meters, completion marks, and compact progress widgets expose basic progress visually.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: End every single lesson on an easier challenge to guarantee a successful, positive final impression.
requirements.assessment: Lab adds an easier final retrieval challenge after the main queue.
requirements.remainingGap: A successful answer cannot be guaranteed; not every canonical lesson uses this final structure.

requirements.userText: Use an aggressively bright, highly saturated color palette to convey energy, excitement, and playfulness.
requirements.assessment: The current friendly interface uses saturated accent colors with light and dark palettes.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Avoid muted, corporate, or overly sophisticated color schemes that detract from the accessible, game-like tone.
requirements.assessment: Bright accents and rounded educational cards establish a playful visual style.
requirements.remainingGap: Aesthetic judgments about corporate or sophisticated tones cannot be established by an executable check.

requirements.userText: Design primary action buttons with a thick, darker-colored bottom border to create a tactile 3D effect.
requirements.assessment: Primary button CSS uses a thick lower border for tactile depth.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Animate buttons upon pressing: shift the button downward and compress the bottom border to simulate physical tactility.
requirements.assessment: Pressed button styles and finite transitions provide tactile feedback.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Round all corners on buttons, cards, and UI elements to make the interface feel friendly, safe, and "juicy".
requirements.assessment: Cards, buttons, dropdowns, and lesson controls have rounded corners.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Keep the interface entirely free of clutter; display only one exercise or concept per screen.
requirements.assessment: Active exercises primarily display one current question or Lab challenge.
requirements.remainingGap: Study libraries and integrated lesson introductions intentionally display several related items.

requirements.userText: Use progressive disclosure: do not show advanced settings or social features until the user has completed the onboarding phase.
requirements.assessment: Advanced controls use disclosures and optional reward onboarding.
requirements.remainingGap: No universal onboarding gate hides all settings or future social controls.

requirements.userText: Provide immediate visual and auditory feedback (e.g., a green screen flash and a happy chime) for every correct answer.
requirements.assessment: Practice feedback pairs a correct state with optional sound cues.
requirements.remainingGap: Full mock answers deliberately receive no correctness feedback before final submission; mute and reduced motion are respected.

requirements.userText: Provide gentle, non-punitive feedback (e.g., a red UI shift and a low tone) for incorrect answers.
requirements.assessment: Incorrect practice answers receive a gentle labeled feedback state and optional low cue.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Never shame the user for failing; frame mistakes as learning opportunities to make failure feel safe.
requirements.assessment: Mistake feedback presents explanations and opportunities to practise again without punishment copy.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Create a central mascot to act as the user's guide, cheerleader, and accountability partner.
requirements.assessment: The original SVG mascot appears in the brand and learning dashboard.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Use the mascot's facial expressions to communicate emotional feedback faster than text.
requirements.assessment: The mascot has a finite user-triggered wave and celebration effects.
requirements.remainingGap: A complete correctness-dependent facial-expression system is not implemented.

requirements.userText: Introduce varied character designs within lessons to "speak" the prompts, adding personality and visual variety.
requirements.assessment: Original prompts and a single mascot provide current lesson presentation.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no illustrated cast of varied speaking lesson characters.

requirements.userText: Implement haptic feedback (vibrations) on mobile devices tied to correct/incorrect answers and button presses.
requirements.assessment: An optional haptics setting prepares supported-device feedback through the app cue integration.
requirements.remainingGap: Vibration API availability differs by device and browser; universal physical vibration is not claimed.

requirements.userText: Support Dark Mode natively, ensuring saturated colors still pop against dark backgrounds.
requirements.assessment: Light and dark themes persist and have native themed study, dropdown, and flashcard styles.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Use vector graphics (SVG/Lottie) for all animations to ensure crisp scaling and small file sizes.
requirements.assessment: Mascot and icons use SVG; lightweight transitions use CSS.
requirements.remainingGap: Not every effect is an SVG or Lottie asset; no Lottie runtime is added.

requirements.userText: Design for single-handed mobile use: place primary navigation and progression buttons at the bottom of the screen.
requirements.assessment: Mobile primary navigation sits at the bottom with safe-area clearance.
requirements.remainingGap: Some exercise actions remain in scrollable content; single-handed usability is not measured for every screen.

requirements.userText: Ensure touch targets are a minimum of 44x44 pixels to prevent accidental mis-taps.
requirements.assessment: Primary controls and drag handles generally use at least 44-pixel minimum dimensions.
requirements.remainingGap: A complete all-elements target-size audit is not performed; sentence tokens currently specify a 44-pixel minimum height.

requirements.userText: Automatically advance to the next question when a user answers a multiple-choice question correctly, saving a tap.
requirements.assessment: Optional automatic advancement follows feedback in micro lessons.
requirements.remainingGap: Canonical exam practice keeps explicit navigation; automatic advance is not forced after every correct answer.

requirements.userText: Ensure the app requires zero instruction manuals; the UI must be inherently intuitive.
requirements.assessment: Visible labels, native semantics, and concise guidance support discovery.
requirements.remainingGap: Zero-instruction intuitiveness requires user testing and cannot be certified from source.

requirements.userText: Remove account creation walls; allow the user to start their first lesson immediately upon opening the app.
requirements.assessment: The local app starts without an account wall or remote authentication.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Ask the user for their primary learning goal (e.g., Travel, Career, School) to personalize the journey context.
requirements.assessment: Optional goal setup asks Travel, Career, or School.
requirements.remainingGap: That preference is recorded for local goals; the content context is not comprehensively personalized to it.

requirements.userText: Ask the user for their current proficiency level to route them to the appropriate starting point.
requirements.assessment: An optional proficiency choice and the global level selector route N5–N1 study.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Provide a short, adaptive placement test for users who claim prior knowledge.
requirements.assessment: Practice can assess the selected level with original questions.
requirements.remainingGap: No short adaptive placement test determines a starting level.

requirements.userText: Make the first lesson exceptionally easy to guarantee a win state and hook the user.
requirements.assessment: A learner can select N5 foundations and a small Lab introduction.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no enforced first-lesson win state or measured first-time difficulty guarantee.

requirements.userText: Introduce the gamification mechanics (XP, Streaks) only *after* the user completes the first lesson.
requirements.assessment: Rewards are optional and can be enabled before or after studying.
requirements.remainingGap: The dashboard may show existing streak information immediately; reward introduction is not tied exclusively to first completion.

requirements.userText: Prompt for account creation (email/password) as a way to "save progress" only after the user has invested effort.
requirements.assessment: Backups save progress without requiring an account.
requirements.remainingGap: Delayed email/password registration and account-based saving are unconnected future work.

requirements.userText: Default to a modest daily goal (e.g., 5-10 minutes) during onboarding to prevent early burnout.
requirements.assessment: Optional motivation defaults to a modest study-minute target.
requirements.remainingGap: The existing action-count goal remains separate and onboarding is not mandatory.

requirements.userText: Request push notification permissions by explaining the exact value (e.g., "Allow notifications so we can remind you to keep your streak").
requirements.assessment: Reminder controls explain open-app browser limitations before requesting permission.
requirements.remainingGap: Scheduled closed-browser push delivery is not supplied and depends on browser or server support.

requirements.userText: Use a soft prompt (custom UI dialog) before triggering the native OS notification permission dialog.
requirements.assessment: A visible explanatory reminder control precedes the native permission request.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Show a visual preview of the learning path during onboarding to set long-term expectations.
requirements.assessment: The learning path is visible on the dashboard and proficiency selection is available.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no separate staged onboarding path-preview screen.

requirements.userText: Grant a small starter bundle of in-app currency to introduce the economy.
requirements.assessment: Coins start from documented learning evidence with no paid purchases.
requirements.remainingGap: A starter currency bundle is not granted merely for onboarding.

requirements.userText: Introduce the mascot immediately as a friendly companion.
requirements.assessment: The original mascot is present from the initial dashboard and brand.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Avoid overwhelming the user with the leaderboard or league systems until day 3 or 4.
requirements.assessment: No leaderboard is displayed or simulated on the local dashboard.
requirements.remainingGap: A day-three or day-four introduction gate requires a future competitive feature.

requirements.userText: Keep the total time from app launch to first completed lesson under 4 minutes.
requirements.assessment: The app permits immediate small lessons with no account setup.
requirements.remainingGap: Launch-to-completion under four minutes has not been measured across users and devices.

requirements.userText: Send daily reminder notifications at the exact time the user usually completes their lessons.
requirements.assessment: An opt-in device reminder uses a chosen local time while the app remains open.
requirements.remainingGap: It does not infer habitual study time or guarantee delivery with the browser closed.

requirements.userText: Utilize the mascot's personality in push notifications (e.g., guilt-tripping, encouraging, or humorous).
requirements.assessment: Reminder copy is encouraging and learner-controlled.
requirements.remainingGap: Guilt-tripping copy is not implemented; support for continued study takes priority over emotional pressure.

requirements.userText: Escalate the urgency of notifications as the day progresses (e.g., friendly morning reminder, urgent evening warning).
requirements.assessment: At most one opted-in local reminder is recorded per day.
requirements.remainingGap: Escalating urgency throughout the day is not implemented.

requirements.userText: Implement a "passive-aggressive" final notification if a user ignores reminders for several days (e.g., "These reminders don't seem to be working. We'll stop sending them for now.") to trigger reverse psychology.
requirements.assessment: Reminders can be paused explicitly without blocking learning.
requirements.remainingGap: Passive-aggressive reverse-psychology notifications are intentionally absent.

requirements.userText: Personalize notifications by including the user's current streak number.
requirements.assessment: Local notification copy may include due recall counts.
requirements.remainingGap: Current streak personalization is not included in the notification body.

requirements.userText: Use rich OS notifications containing dynamic images of the mascot.
requirements.assessment: The mascot is a bundled SVG asset.
requirements.remainingGap: Dynamic-image rich OS notifications are not implemented and platform support varies.

requirements.userText: Send a celebratory email or push notification when a user hits a milestone (e.g., 7-day streak, 100 days).
requirements.assessment: Local badges and milestone rewards are visible within the app.
requirements.remainingGap: No celebratory email or backend push service is connected.

requirements.userText: Introduce a "Month Long Challenge" with a unique badge to encourage consistent 30-day engagement.
requirements.assessment: A monthly local learning quest grants a reward and badge.
requirements.remainingGap: The current requirement is 300 XP and five active days, not mandatory thirty-day engagement.

requirements.userText: Run special weekend events (e.g., XP multipliers) to boost engagement during historically low-traffic days.
requirements.assessment: Earned boosts are local and explicitly activated.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no weekend event scheduler or live-ops service.

requirements.userText: Send personalized weekly recap emails detailing XP earned, words learned, and accuracy rate.
requirements.assessment: Local history and reward receipts provide in-app progress context.
requirements.remainingGap: No weekly recap email, recipient account, or mail service is connected.

requirements.userText: Monitor user drop-off points in the curriculum and dynamically adjust the difficulty curve to smooth out friction.
requirements.assessment: Local mistakes and latency records support review and weak-question prioritization.
requirements.remainingGap: No aggregate drop-off analytics pipeline dynamically adjusts the curriculum curve.

requirements.userText: Implement win-back campaigns for churned users offering a "Streak Repair" if they return within a specific window.
requirements.assessment: Freeze protection is earned locally rather than linked to a return campaign.
requirements.remainingGap: No churn-targeted repair campaign or pressure window is implemented.

requirements.userText: Use deep linking in all notifications to drop the user directly into a lesson, bypassing the home screen.
requirements.assessment: Local reminders can open review or practice and a daily lesson has a saved resume point.
requirements.remainingGap: No hosted notification deep-link service targets every specific unfinished lesson.

requirements.userText: Implement home screen widgets (iOS/Android) that visually display the user's daily streak status.
requirements.assessment: Home widgets are customizable cards inside the web app.
requirements.remainingGap: No native iOS or Android home-screen widget integration is supplied.

requirements.userText: Vary notification copy daily; never send the exact same text two days in a row.

requirements.remainingGap: An unlockable preapproved avatar catalog is absent; removing uploads does not by itself eliminate all moderation needs.

requirements.userText: Implement a privacy toggle to completely opt-out of Leagues and Leaderboards, making the user's profile private and invisible to strangers.
requirements.assessment: Progress and the optional badge shelf remain private on the device. Users explicitly choose a summary export that excludes individual answers, content IDs, study dates, voice preferences, and personal text.

evidence.anchor: a stale confirmation refuses to erase notes changed after review

requirements.remainingGap: There is no live league service or public profile to opt out of, and no shared-profile visibility toggle is implemented. Exported files remain under the user's own control.

requirements.userText: Use an LLM API (like Google Gemini) asynchronously in the backend to generate dynamic explanations for *why* a user's specific typed answer was wrong.
requirements.assessment: Authored deterministic explanations are stored locally.
requirements.remainingGap: No LLM API, backend prompt service, or personalized incorrect-answer explanation is connected.

requirements.userText: Cache these LLM-generated explanations by hashing the `(Prompt_ID + User_Incorrect_Answer)` to avoid calling the LLM API twice for the exact same common mistake.
requirements.assessment: Static explanations avoid repeated external generation requests.
requirements.remainingGap: No prompt/incorrect-answer hash cache or LLM request store exists.

requirements.userText: Ensure the LLM prompt for generating feedback explicitly enforces a strict character limit (e.g., max 150 characters) so the explanation fits perfectly in the mobile UI modal.
requirements.assessment: Current explanations are authored text that can wrap in the interface.
requirements.remainingGap: No LLM prompt-length policy or generated 150-character validator is implemented.

requirements.userText: Instruct the LLM to adopt the persona of the app's mascot when generating error explanations (e.g., keeping a cheerful, encouraging tone).
requirements.assessment: The mascot and authored feedback use current local copy.
requirements.remainingGap: No LLM persona prompt or generated feedback service is connected.

requirements.userText: Provide a "Generate More Examples" button on grammar rules that queries an LLM to generate 3 brand new, personalized sentences based on the user's stated interests (e.g., programming, gaming).
requirements.assessment: Grammar panels provide original authored examples.
requirements.remainingGap: No personalized Generate More Examples API or interest-conditioned model request is supplied.

requirements.userText: Add a safeguard layer validating that any LLM-generated Japanese sentence contains valid N5-N3 Kanji before presenting it to the user.
requirements.assessment: Deterministic content checks validate the original bank's structural integrity.
requirements.remainingGap: No LLM output guard validates a complete N5–N3 Kanji inventory; the requested narrower gate also differs from the app's N1/N2 scope.

requirements.userText: Do not use LLMs for evaluating the correctness of standard multiple-choice or exact-match questions; rely on deterministic string matching for speed, cost-efficiency, and reliability.
requirements.assessment: Canonical choice grading uses explicit option IDs and Lab exact recall uses deterministic normalization.
requirements.remainingGap: None within the stated scope.

requirements.userText: Use LLMs to dynamically generate short, culturally accurate reading comprehension stories based *only* on the specific vocabulary pool the user has already unlocked.
requirements.assessment: Reading passages are original authored static records with explicit question evidence.
requirements.remainingGap: No vocabulary-restricted LLM story generator or cultural-review pipeline is connected.

requirements.userText: Programmatically strip out any Romaji from LLM-generated Japanese text before storing it in the database, relying exclusively on your own Furigana generation script for consistency.
requirements.assessment: Canonical Japanese text does not require stored romaji fields.
requirements.remainingGap: There is no LLM text-ingestion pipeline, automated romaji stripping, or comprehensive generated furigana service.

requirements.userText: Implement an admin-only "Regenerate Audio" script that uses the latest neural Text-to-Speech models to automatically update all audio files if a better, more natural voice model is released.
requirements.assessment: The browser offers available Japanese voices and optional original-script synthesis.
requirements.remainingGap: No authenticated administrator audio-regeneration job, neural TTS provider, or recording-library migration is connected.
